findings.reason: the section rewrites the shared claim-resolution path every one of those importers exercises, so a builder following this population can redden a file the gate never runs and still report 0 added failures, which is the exact silent-landing defect §19 was written to repair; the population should read "the test files importing `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`", as §18's gate does.
findings.text: §20's gate names `tests/test_a_node_is_queued_once.py` as a file that "show[s] no added failure against base", but that module does not import `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` (it imports `reckon.crew.dispatch_admission`), while six modules that do import it are omitted: `tests/test_a_discarded_request_stays_discarded.py`, `tests/test_a_held_request_stays_queued.py`, `tests/test_a_jev_hold_queues_for_the_local_lane.py`, `tests/test_a_queued_plan_review_is_stored.py`, `tests/test_a_queued_plan_review_keeps_its_brief.py`, `tests/test_a_review_is_not_refused_for_its_run.py`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `_earlier_overlapping_request` and `_queued_requests_overlap` at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:270,250`, `_pointer_scope_entries` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:222`, `runs._scopes_overlap` at `reckon/crew/runs.py:780`, `_publish_transitions` and `_assert_clean` at `tests/test_refused_dispatch_leaves_no_pointer.py:230,253`, and the named case at that file line 374.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §20's gate population names a file that does not import the module it changes and omits six files that do, so the gate can read clean while an importer breaks.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections log the case and the control "under the run directory", a durable path that outlives the run.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol, filename or comment; §20 and §21 name mechanisms only.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the quadratic cost §20 blames is in the cited code, not argued past it: `_queued_requests_overlap` calls `_resolved_request_claims` on each side per comparison, and `admit_once` calls the pre-check once per request against `order[:index]`, giving the ~N(N−1) resolutions the section describes; §21's premise verifiably holds, the landed case never calls `_publish_transitions`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §20 names one mechanism (one claim resolution per request per pass) and §21 one (the refusal case's watch-row assertion), each with its own case and control.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §20's only dependency is §18's overlap pre-check, which has landed, and §21 edits only the file §19 landed; the new followup `f-ahdwft-s20-s21` states correctly that the two share no file and may dispatch together.
